module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 512

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/512](https://www.erdosproblems.com/512)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl.
  (1961), 221-254.
- [Ko81] Konyagin, S. V., *On the Littlewood problem*. Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. (1981),
  243-265, 463.
- [MPS81] McGehee, O. Carruth and Pigno, Louis and Smith, Brent, *Hardy's inequality and the
  $L^1$ norm of exponential sums*. Ann. of Math. (2) (1981), 613-618.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped ExponentialSum

namespace Erdos512

/--
Is it true that, if $A\subset \mathbb{Z}$ is a finite set of size $N$, then
$$\int_0^1 \left\lvert \sum_{n\in A}e(n\theta)\right\rvert \mathrm{d}\theta \gg \log N,$$
where $e(x)=e^{2\pi ix }$?

Littlewood's conjecture, proved independently by Konyagin [Ko81] and McGehee, Pigno, and
Smith [MPS81].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 42, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/f8a51976fd2e66a52b4928c109fb9ae877a1a507/problems/512/Erdos512.lean"]
theorem erdos_512 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℤ), A.card = N →
      c * Real.log N ≤ ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖∑ n ∈ A, e (n * θ)‖ := by
  sorry

end Erdos512

reformulations.difference: Lean includes N = 0, whereas the informal logarithmic bound is conventionally read for positive cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: When N = 0, A.card = N forces A = ∅. Mathlib's Real.log 0 is 0, the empty exponential sum is 0, and its integral is 0. Thus the added case is exactly 0 ≤ 0 and imposes no constraint on the positive constant. The statement is equivalent to restricting N to positive integers; this equivalence was proved directly in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/512 — statement, remarks, and affirmative PROVED (LEAN) status; read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/512.

Konyagin, On a problem of Littlewood, English translation in Math. USSR Izvestiya 18 (1982), 205–225; introduction, main theorem, and corollaries: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/IM1982v018n02ABEH001386/pdf.
McGehee–Pigno–Smith, Hardy's inequality and the L¹-norm of exponential sums (1981), publisher bibliographic record: https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1981/113-3/p09.

O. Carruth McGehee, Remarks on the Littlewood Conjecture (1993), statement, settlement history, and proof exposition: https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mcgehee/LittlewoodConj93.pdf; linked from https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mcgehee/.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully expresses the source's uniform lower bound: the positive constant precedes both universal quantifiers, the exponential notation has the correct normalization, and the complex norm is the intended modulus. Lean checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verify continuity and interval integrability, empty and singleton cases, and equivalence with the linked external theorem. All scratch checks pass. The affirmative answer and research solved tag agree with the source. The external proof contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms, but replay encountered compatibility/elaboration errors with the supplied Mathlib; its original proof environment was not independently revalidated.
